hints: The particle starts from rest with acceleration $a(t) = 0.6t$ for $0 \le t \le 4$.
Evaluate at $t = 4$ to show that $V = 0.3(4^2) = 4.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Integrate acceleration $a = 0.6t$ with initial rest condition $v(0) = 0$:
$$v(t) = \int 0.6t\,dt = 0.3t^2$$

Substitute $t = 4$ to obtain the speed V:
$$V = 0.3(4^2) = 0.3(16) = 4.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Integrate acceleration with respect to time for the first interval $0 \le t \le 4$:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt = \int 0.6t\,dt = 0.3t^2 + c$$

The particle starts from rest at $t = 0$, so $v(0) = 0 \implies c = 0$:
$$v(t) = 0.3t^2$$
This verifies that $V = 4.8$.

hints: Stage 1 ($0 \le t \le 4$): a quadratic curve curving upwards from $(0,0)$ to $(4, 4.8)$.
Stage 2 ($4 \le t \le 15$): a horizontal line segment from $(4, 4.8)$ to $(15, 4.8)$.
Stage 3 ($15 \le t \le 20$): a straight line sloping downwards from $(15, 4.8)$ to $(20, 0)$.
walkthrough:
Sketch the velocity-time graph in three distinct sections:
$$\text{1. A quadratic curve starting at } (0,0) \text{ curving upwards to } (4, 4.8)$$
$$\text{2. A horizontal straight line from } (4, 4.8) \text{ to } (15, 4.8)$$
$$\text{3. A straight line decelerating from } (15, 4.8) \text{ down to } (20, 0) \text{ on the time axis}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Draw coordinate axes with $t$ on the horizontal axis and $v$ on the vertical axis.
1. From $t = 0$ to $t = 4$, $v = 0.3t^2$: this is a concave-up quadratic curve starting at $(0,0)$ with zero gradient and rising to $(4, 4.8)$.
2. From $t = 4$ to $t = 15$, the particle moves at constant speed: draw a horizontal straight line at height $v = 4.8$ from $t = 4$ to $t = 15$.
3. From $t = 15$ to $t = 20$, the particle decelerates uniformly to rest: draw a straight line segment with negative slope connecting $(15, 4.8)$ to $(20, 0)$.

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Draws quadratic curve from (0,0) to (4,4.8), horizontal line to (15,4.8), and straight line to (20,0).

hints: For $15 \le t \le 20$, the velocity decreases linearly from $4.8$ at $t = 15$ to $0$ at $t = 20$.
Calculate the constant acceleration: $a = \frac{0 - 4.8}{20 - 15} = -\frac{4.8}{5} = -0.96\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use the equation of the line $v - 0 = -0.96(t - 20)$ to express $v$ in terms of $t$.
walkthrough:
Find the constant acceleration during the deceleration phase from $t = 15$ to $t = 20$:
$$a = \frac{0 - 4.8}{20 - 15} = \frac{-4.8}{5} = -0.96\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Write the linear velocity function using $v(20) = 0$:
$$v(t) = 0 - 0.96(t - 20) = 19.2 - 0.96t\quad(\text{or } 9.2 - 0.96t\text{ from MS})$$
$$\text{Check: } -0.96(t - 20) = 19.2 - 0.96t; \text{ at } t=15, 19.2 - 0.96(15) = 19.2 - 14.4 = 4.8$$
$$\text{Expression: } v(t) = 19.2 - 0.96t$$
teacher_walkthrough: For the time interval $15 \le t \le 20$, the particle undergoes constant deceleration from $v = 4.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Step 1: Determine the constant acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{0 - 4.8}{20 - 15} = -\frac{4.8}{5} = -0.96\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Step 2: Use the point-slope form of the linear equation passing through $(20, 0)$:
$$v(t) - 0 = a(t - 20)$$
$$v(t) = -0.96(t - 20)$$
$$v(t) = -0.96t + 19.2 = 19.2 - 0.96t$$
Verify at $t = 15$: $v(15) = 19.2 - 0.96(15) = 19.2 - 14.4 = 4.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which correctly matches the speed at $t = 15$.
Thus, the expression for velocity is $v(t) = 19.2 - 0.96t$ (or $v = -0.96t + 19.2$).

hints: Divide the motion into three stages: Stage 1 ($0$ to $4\text{ s}$), Stage 2 ($4$ to $15\text{ s}$), and Stage 3 ($15$ to $20\text{ s}$).
For Stage 2 (constant speed), area is rectangle: $s_2 = 4.8 \times (15 - 4) = 4.8 \times 11 = 52.8\text{ m}$.
For Stage 3, area is triangle: $s_3 = \frac{1}{2}(5)(4.8) = 12\text{ m}$.
Add the three distances together to find the total distance.
walkthrough:
Calculate the distance in Stage 1 by integration:
$$s_1 = \int_0^4 0.3t^2 dt = \left[0.1t^3\right]_0^4 = 0.1(64) = 6.4\text{ m}$$

Calculate the distance in Stage 2 (rectangle from $t = 4$ to $t = 15$):
$$s_2 = 4.8 \times (15 - 4) = 4.8 \times 11 = 52.8\text{ m}$$

Calculate the distance in Stage 3 (triangle from $t = 15$ to $t = 20$):
$$s_3 = \frac{1}{2}(20 - 15)(4.8) = 0.5(5)(4.8) = 12\text{ m}$$

Sum the distances to find the total distance:
$$\text{Total distance} = 6.4 + 52.8 + 12 = 71.2\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: To find the total distance travelled, sum the areas under the velocity-time graph across all three stages:
Step 1: First phase ($0 \le t \le 4$).

Here $v = 0.3t^2$, so we evaluate the definite integral:
$$s_1 = \int_0^4 0.3t^2\,dt = \left[0.1t^3\right]_0^4 = 0.1(4^3) - 0 = 0.1(64) = 6.4\text{ m}$$
Step 2: Second phase ($4 \le t \le 15$).

The velocity is constant at $4.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ over a duration of $\Delta t = 15 - 4 = 11\text{ s}$:
$$s_2 = 4.8 \times 11 = 52.8\text{ m}$$
Step 3: Third phase ($15 \le t \le 20$).

The velocity decreases linearly to zero over a duration of $\Delta t = 20 - 15 = 5\text{ s}$. The area of this triangular region is:
$$s_3 = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4.8 = 12\text{ m}$$

Step 4: Total distance:
$$\text{Total distance} = s_1 + s_2 + s_3 = 6.4 + 52.8 + 12 = 71.2\text{ m}$$
Therefore, the total distance travelled by the particle is $71.2\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Integrates $0.3t^2$ to get $6.4\text{ m}$, computes middle and end areas $52.8\text{ m}$ and $12\text{ m}$, yielding total distance $= 71.2\text{ m}$.
